description: A statement that runs the first block whose condition is `true`, checking the conditions from top to bottom.
An `if` at the start of a method that returns early for a special case, so the rest of the method handles only the normal case.
An expression that picks one of two values, as in `count == 1 ? "item" : "items"`.
A statement that compares one value against constant `case` labels, where every section must end with `break` or `return`.
Loops that repeat a block while a condition is `true`; `for` puts the start, the condition and the step in one line.
A loop that visits every element of an array or collection in order, without an index.
A fixed number of values of one type, such as `int[]`, read by an index from `0` to `Length - 1`.
A loop or comparison that is wrong by one step, such as `i <= values.Length`, which reads past the end of an array.
